notes: IBM has no victim reports. Each test-day laundering attempt stands in for one: the trace starts from the account that made the attempt's first payment, at that payment's time, naming its amount.
Each trace runs on the live engine's state at the stated delay after that first payment, as POST /trace would. It can only follow payments inside the engine's 72-hour window and one bank's view.

The reported first payment is always where the trace starts, so it is not scored. located_later_share is the share of the attempt's later money (paid by the stated delay) that the trail contains; located_reachable_share counts only later payments a forward trace could reach at all (the first payer's own later payments, and payments by accounts the attempt's money had reached). Fan-in and bipartite attempts have many payers, most of them unreachable from one report.
Two report styles are compared: naming the paid amount (the trace starts from the 3 closest payments) and naming none (it starts from every payment to a new payee from that time).
trail_precision is the share of the trail's payments that are laundering of any attempt.

held_low and held_high are the liens the plan proposes under the three tracing rules (haircut, FIFO, LIBR), as shares of the money traced into the trail. top_k_held_share uses each lien's lowest figure.
IBM amounts are in US dollars.
